For [GTIN](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/technical/idkeys/gtin)-related fields, see [Check Digit calculator](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/support/check_digit_calculator) and [validation guide](http://www.gs1us.org/resources/standards/gtin-validation-guide) from [GS1](http://www.gs1.org/).

@graph.rdfs:label: WPAdBlock
@graph.name: WPAdBlock
@graph.rdfs:comment: An advertising section of the page.

@graph.rdfs:label: Physician
@graph.name: Physician
@graph.rdfs:comment: An individual physician or a physician's office considered as a [[MedicalOrganization]].

@graph.rdfs:label: rsvpResponse
@graph.name: rsvpResponse
@graph.rdfs:comment: The response (yes, no, maybe) to the RSVP.

@graph.rdfs:label: FoodEvent
@graph.name: FoodEvent
@graph.rdfs:comment: Event type: Food event.

@graph.rdfs:label: TouristAttraction
@graph.name: TouristAttraction
@graph.rdfs:comment: A tourist attraction.  In principle any Thing can be a [[TouristAttraction]], from a [[Mountain]] and [[LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings]] to a [[LocalBusiness]].  This Type can be used on its own to describe a general [[TouristAttraction]], or be used as an [[additionalType]] to add tourist attraction properties to any other type.  (See examples below)

@graph.rdfs:label: disambiguatingDescription
@graph.name: disambiguatingDescription
@graph.rdfs:comment: A sub property of description. A short description of the item used to disambiguate from other, similar items. Information from other properties (in particular, name) may be necessary for the description to be useful for disambiguation.

@graph.rdfs:label: WearableSizeSystemEnumeration
@graph.name: WearableSizeSystemEnumeration
@graph.rdfs:comment: Enumerates common size systems specific for wearable products.

@graph.rdfs:label: playersOnline
@graph.name: playersOnline
@graph.rdfs:comment: Number of players on the server.

@graph.rdfs:label: ReviewNewsArticle
@graph.name: ReviewNewsArticle
@graph.rdfs:comment: A [[NewsArticle]] and [[CriticReview]] providing a professional critic's assessment of a service, product, performance, or artistic or literary work.

@graph.rdfs:label: Drawing
@graph.name: Drawing
@graph.rdfs:comment: A picture or diagram made with a pencil, pen, or crayon rather than paint.

@graph.rdfs:label: breadcrumb
@graph.name: breadcrumb
@graph.rdfs:comment: A set of links that can help a user understand and navigate a website hierarchy.

@graph.rdfs:label: actionProcess
@graph.name: actionProcess
@graph.rdfs:comment: Description of the process by which the action was performed.

@graph.rdfs:label: RadioClip
@graph.name: RadioClip
@graph.rdfs:comment: A short radio program or a segment/part of a radio program.

@graph.rdfs:label: countriesNotSupported
@graph.name: countriesNotSupported
@graph.rdfs:comment: Countries for which the application is not supported. You can also provide the two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code.

@graph.rdfs:label: Duration
@graph.name: Duration
@graph.rdfs:comment: Quantity: Duration (use [ISO 8601 duration format](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601)).

@graph.rdfs:label: maintainer
@graph.name: maintainer
@graph.rdfs:comment: A maintainer of a [[Dataset]], software package ([[SoftwareApplication]]), or other [[Project]]. A maintainer is a [[Person]] or [[Organization]] that manages contributions to, and/or publication of, some (typically complex) artifact. It is common for distributions of software and data to be based on "upstream" sources. When [[maintainer]] is applied to a specific version of something e.g. a particular version or packaging of a [[Dataset]], it is always  possible that the upstream source has a different maintainer. The [[isBasedOn]] property can be used to indicate such relationships between datasets to make the different maintenance roles clear. Similarly in the case of software, a package may have dedicated maintainers working on integration into software distributions such as Ubuntu, as well as upstream maintainers of the underlying work.

@graph.rdfs:label: bankAccountType
@graph.name: bankAccountType
@graph.rdfs:comment: The type of a bank account.

@graph.rdfs:label: ProductGroup
@graph.name: ProductGroup
@graph.rdfs:comment:
A ProductGroup represents a group of [[Product]]s that vary only in certain well-described ways, such as by [[size]], [[color]], [[material]] etc.

While a ProductGroup itself is not directly offered for sale, the various varying products that it represents can be. The ProductGroup serves as a prototype or template, standing in for all of the products who have an [[isVariantOf]] relationship to it. As such, properties (including additional types) can be applied to the ProductGroup to represent characteristics shared by each of the (possibly very many) variants. Properties that reference a ProductGroup are not included in this mechanism; neither are the following specific properties [[variesBy]], [[hasVariant]], [[url]].

@graph.rdfs:label: stage
@graph.name: stage
@graph.rdfs:comment: The stage of the condition, if applicable.

@graph.rdfs:label: vatID
@graph.name: vatID
@graph.rdfs:comment: The value-added Tax ID of the organization or person with national prefix (for example IT123456789). Can also be described as [[iso6523Code]] with proper prefix.

@graph.rdfs:label: device
@graph.name: device
@graph.rdfs:comment: Device required to run the application. Used in cases where a specific make/model is required to run the application.

@graph.rdfs:label: Menu
@graph.name: Menu
@graph.rdfs:comment: A structured representation of food or drink items available from a FoodEstablishment.

@graph.rdfs:label: Rating
@graph.name: Rating
@graph.rdfs:comment: A rating is an evaluation on a numeric scale, such as 1 to 5 stars.

@graph.rdfs:label: ReservationStatusType
@graph.name: ReservationStatusType
@graph.rdfs:comment: Enumerated status values for Reservation.

@graph.rdfs:label: employmentType
@graph.name: employmentType
@graph.rdfs:comment: Type of employment (e.g. full-time, part-time, contract, temporary, seasonal, internship).

@graph.rdfs:label: recommendedIntake
@graph.name: recommendedIntake
@graph.rdfs:comment: Recommended intake of this supplement for a given population as defined by a specific recommending authority.

@graph.rdfs:label: termsPerYear
@graph.name: termsPerYear
@graph.rdfs:comment: The number of times terms of study are offered per year. Semesters and quarters are common units for term. For example, if the student can only take 2 semesters for the program in one year, then termsPerYear should be 2.

@graph.rdfs:label: issueNumber
@graph.name: issueNumber
@graph.rdfs:comment: Identifies the issue of publication; for example, "iii" or "2".

@graph.rdfs:label: landlord
@graph.name: landlord
@graph.rdfs:comment: A sub property of participant. The owner of the real estate property.

@graph.rdfs:label: lyricist
@graph.name: lyricist
@graph.rdfs:comment: The person who wrote the words.

@graph.rdfs:label: expertConsiderations
@graph.name: expertConsiderations
@graph.rdfs:comment: Medical expert advice related to the plan.

@graph.rdfs:label: alcoholWarning
@graph.name: alcoholWarning
@graph.rdfs:comment: Any precaution, guidance, contraindication, etc. related to consumption of alcohol while taking this drug.

@graph.rdfs:label: isBasedOn
@graph.name: isBasedOn
@graph.rdfs:comment: A resource from which this work is derived or from which it is a modification or adaptation.

@graph.rdfs:label: GameServer
@graph.name: GameServer
@graph.rdfs:comment: Server that provides game interaction in a multiplayer game.

@graph.rdfs:label: permissionType
@graph.name: permissionType
@graph.rdfs:comment: The type of permission granted the person, organization, or audience.

@graph.rdfs:label: HotelRoom
@graph.name: HotelRoom
@graph.rdfs:comment:
A hotel room is a single room in a hotel.

See also the dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations.

@graph.rdfs:label: Motorcycle
@graph.name: Motorcycle
@graph.rdfs:comment: A motorcycle or motorbike is a single-track, two-wheeled motor vehicle.

@graph.rdfs:label: OceanBodyOfWater
@graph.name: OceanBodyOfWater
@graph.rdfs:comment: An ocean (for example, the Pacific).

@graph.rdfs:label: sizeSystem
@graph.name: sizeSystem
@graph.rdfs:comment: The size system used to identify a product's size. Typically either a standard (for example, "GS1" or "ISO-EN13402"), country code (for example "US" or "JP"), or a measuring system (for example "Metric" or "Imperial").

@graph.rdfs:label: numItems
@graph.name: numItems
@graph.rdfs:comment: Limits the number of items being shipped for which these conditions apply.

@graph.rdfs:label: MusicGroup
@graph.name: MusicGroup
@graph.rdfs:comment: A musical group, such as a band, an orchestra, or a choir. Can also be a solo musician.

@graph.rdfs:label: RealEstateAgent
@graph.name: RealEstateAgent
@graph.rdfs:comment: A real-estate agent.

@graph.rdfs:label: HealthInsurancePlan
@graph.name: HealthInsurancePlan
@graph.rdfs:comment: A US-style health insurance plan, including PPOs, EPOs, and HMOs.

@graph.rdfs:label: antagonist
@graph.name: antagonist
@graph.rdfs:comment: The muscle whose action counteracts the specified muscle.

@graph.rdfs:label: DepartmentStore
@graph.name: DepartmentStore
@graph.rdfs:comment: A department store.

@graph.rdfs:label: AnatomicalSystem
@graph.name: AnatomicalSystem
@graph.rdfs:comment: An anatomical system is a group of anatomical structures that work together to perform a certain task. Anatomical systems, such as organ systems, are one organizing principle of anatomy, and can include circulatory, digestive, endocrine, integumentary, immune, lymphatic, muscular, nervous, reproductive, respiratory, skeletal, urinary, vestibular, and other systems.

@graph.rdfs:label: Locksmith
@graph.name: Locksmith
@graph.rdfs:comment: A locksmith.

@graph.rdfs:label: transmissionMethod
@graph.name: transmissionMethod
@graph.rdfs:comment: How the disease spreads, either as a route or vector, for example 'direct contact', 'Aedes aegypti', etc.

@graph.rdfs:label: MotorizedBicycle
@graph.name: MotorizedBicycle
@graph.rdfs:comment: A motorized bicycle is a bicycle with an attached motor used to power the vehicle, or to assist with pedaling.

@graph.rdfs:label: courseMode
@graph.name: courseMode
@graph.rdfs:comment: The medium or means of delivery of the course instance or the mode of study, either as a text label (e.g. "online", "onsite" or "blended"; "synchronous" or "asynchronous"; "full-time" or "part-time") or as a URL reference to a term from a controlled vocabulary (e.g. https://ceds.ed.gov/element/001311#Asynchronous).

@graph.rdfs:label: Blog
@graph.name: Blog
@graph.rdfs:comment: A [blog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blog), sometimes known as a "weblog". Note that the individual posts ([[BlogPosting]]s) in a [[Blog]] are often colloquially referred to by the same term.

@graph.rdfs:label: orderNumber
@graph.name: orderNumber
@graph.rdfs:comment: The identifier of the transaction.

@graph.rdfs:label: Chapter
@graph.name: Chapter
@graph.rdfs:comment: One of the sections into which a book is divided. A chapter usually has a section number or a name.

@graph.rdfs:label: AssignAction
@graph.name: AssignAction
@graph.rdfs:comment: The act of allocating an action/event/task to some destination (someone or something).

@graph.rdfs:label: subtitleLanguage
@graph.name: subtitleLanguage
@graph.rdfs:comment: Languages in which subtitles/captions are available, in [IETF BCP 47 standard format](http://tools.ietf.org/html/bcp47).

@graph.rdfs:label: UserComments
@graph.name: UserComments
@graph.rdfs:comment: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use [[Action]]-based vocabulary, alongside types such as [[Comment]].

@graph.rdfs:label: DrugPrescriptionStatus
@graph.name: DrugPrescriptionStatus
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indicates whether this drug is available by prescription or over-the-counter.

@graph.rdfs:label: SuperficialAnatomy
@graph.name: SuperficialAnatomy
@graph.rdfs:comment: Anatomical features that can be observed by sight (without dissection), including the form and proportions of the human body as well as surface landmarks that correspond to deeper subcutaneous structures. Superficial anatomy plays an important role in sports medicine, phlebotomy, and other medical specialties as underlying anatomical structures can be identified through surface palpation. For example, during back surgery, superficial anatomy can be used to palpate and count vertebrae to find the site of incision. Or in phlebotomy, superficial anatomy can be used to locate an underlying vein; for example, the median cubital vein can be located by palpating the borders of the cubital fossa (such as the epicondyles of the humerus) and then looking for the superficial signs of the vein, such as size, prominence, ability to refill after depression, and feel of surrounding tissue support. As another example, in a subluxation (dislocation) of the glenohumeral joint, the bony structure becomes pronounced with the deltoid muscle failing to cover the glenohumeral joint allowing the edges of the scapula to be superficially visible. Here, the superficial anatomy is the visible edges of the scapula, implying the underlying dislocation of the joint (the related anatomical structure).

@graph.rdfs:label: ParentAudience
@graph.name: ParentAudience
@graph.rdfs:comment: A set of characteristics describing parents, who can be interested in viewing some content.

@graph.rdfs:label: BroadcastService
@graph.name: BroadcastService
@graph.rdfs:comment: A delivery service through which content is provided via broadcast over the air or online.

@graph.rdfs:label: LoanOrCredit
@graph.name: LoanOrCredit
@graph.rdfs:comment: A financial product for the loaning of an amount of money, or line of credit, under agreed terms and charges.

@graph.rdfs:label: codeSampleType
@graph.name: codeSampleType
@graph.rdfs:comment: What type of code sample: full (compile ready) solution, code snippet, inline code, scripts, template.

@graph.rdfs:label: Permit
@graph.name: Permit
@graph.rdfs:comment: A permit issued by an organization, e.g. a parking pass.

@graph.rdfs:label: MeetingRoom
@graph.name: MeetingRoom
@graph.rdfs:comment:
A meeting room, conference room, or conference hall is a room provided for singular events such as business conferences and meetings (source: Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia, see http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conference_hall).

See also the dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations.

@graph.rdfs:label: DefinedTerm
@graph.name: DefinedTerm
@graph.rdfs:comment: A word, name, acronym, phrase, etc. with a formal definition. Often used in the context of category or subject classification, glossaries or dictionaries, product or creative work types, etc. Use the name property for the term being defined, use termCode if the term has an alpha-numeric code allocated, use description to provide the definition of the term. Use the about property to specify what the term is about.

@graph.rdfs:label: familyName
@graph.name: familyName
@graph.rdfs:comment: Family name. In the U.S., the last name of a Person.

@graph.rdfs:label: medicalSpecialty
@graph.name: medicalSpecialty
@graph.rdfs:comment: A medical specialty of the provider.

@graph.rdfs:label: weightPercentage
@graph.name: weightPercentage
@graph.rdfs:comment: Value representing the fraction of the weight that is used to compute the shipping price. Example: 0.10 and a shipping weight of 15kg would add $1.5 to the order price, where the $ is the currency of the order.

@graph.rdfs:label: colorist
@graph.name: colorist
@graph.rdfs:comment: The individual who adds color to inked drawings.

@graph.rdfs:label: mileageFromOdometer
@graph.name: mileageFromOdometer
@graph.rdfs:comment: The total distance travelled by the particular vehicle since its initial production, as read from its odometer.\n\nTypical unit code(s): KMT for kilometers, SMI for statute miles.

@graph.rdfs:label: studySubject
@graph.name: studySubject
@graph.rdfs:comment: A subject of the study, i.e. one of the medical conditions, therapies, devices, drugs, etc. investigated by the study.

@graph.rdfs:label: claimReviewed
@graph.name: claimReviewed
@graph.rdfs:comment: A short summary of the specific claims reviewed in a ClaimReview.

@graph.rdfs:label: geoCoveredBy
@graph.name: geoCoveredBy
@graph.rdfs:comment: Represents a relationship between two geometries (or the places they represent), relating a geometry to another that covers it. As defined in [DE-9IM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DE-9IM).

@graph.rdfs:label: orderItemNumber
@graph.name: orderItemNumber
@graph.rdfs:comment: The identifier of the order item.

@graph.rdfs:label: doorTime
@graph.name: doorTime
@graph.rdfs:comment: The time admission will commence.

@graph.rdfs:label: FastFoodRestaurant
@graph.name: FastFoodRestaurant
@graph.rdfs:comment: A fast-food restaurant.

@graph.rdfs:label: color
@graph.name: color
@graph.rdfs:comment: The color of the product.

@graph.rdfs:label: bookingTime
@graph.name: bookingTime
@graph.rdfs:comment: The date and time the reservation was booked.

@graph.rdfs:label: EmployeeRole
@graph.name: EmployeeRole
@graph.rdfs:comment: A subclass of OrganizationRole used to describe employee relationships.

@graph.rdfs:label: GeoCoordinates
@graph.name: GeoCoordinates
@graph.rdfs:comment: The geographic coordinates of a place or event.

@graph.rdfs:label: serverStatus
@graph.name: serverStatus
@graph.rdfs:comment: Status of a game server.

@graph.rdfs:label: courseCode
@graph.name: courseCode
@graph.rdfs:comment: The identifier for the [[Course]] used by the course [[provider]] (e.g. CS101 or 6.001).

@graph.rdfs:label: HowToItem
@graph.name: HowToItem
@graph.rdfs:comment: An item used as either a tool or supply when performing the instructions for how to achieve a result.

@graph.rdfs:label: AnimalShelter
@graph.name: AnimalShelter
@graph.rdfs:comment: Animal shelter.

@graph.rdfs:label: codingSystem
@graph.name: codingSystem
@graph.rdfs:comment: The coding system, e.g. 'ICD-10'.

@graph.rdfs:label: BookmarkAction
@graph.name: BookmarkAction
@graph.rdfs:comment: An agent bookmarks/flags/labels/tags/marks an object.

@graph.rdfs:label: isBasedOnUrl
@graph.name: isBasedOnUrl
@graph.rdfs:comment: A resource that was used in the creation of this resource. This term can be repeated for multiple sources. For example, http://example.com/great-multiplication-intro.html.

@graph.rdfs:label: driveWheelConfiguration
@graph.name: driveWheelConfiguration
@graph.rdfs:comment: The drive wheel configuration, i.e. which roadwheels will receive torque from the vehicle's engine via the drivetrain.

@graph.rdfs:label: LikeAction
@graph.name: LikeAction
@graph.rdfs:comment: The act of expressing a positive sentiment about the object. An agent likes an object (a proposition, topic or theme) with participants.

@graph.rdfs:label: IncentiveType
@graph.name: IncentiveType
@graph.rdfs:comment: Enumerates common financial incentives for products, including tax credits, tax deductions, rebates and subsidies, etc.

@graph.rdfs:label: followee
@graph.name: followee
@graph.rdfs:comment: A sub property of object. The person or organization being followed.

@graph.rdfs:label: object
@graph.name: object
@graph.rdfs:comment: The object upon which the action is carried out, whose state is kept intact or changed. Also known as the semantic roles patient, affected or undergoer (which change their state) or theme (which doesn't). E.g. John read *a book*.

@graph.rdfs:label: ethicsPolicy
@graph.name: ethicsPolicy
@graph.rdfs:comment: Statement about ethics policy, e.g. of a [[NewsMediaOrganization]] regarding journalistic and publishing practices, or of a [[Restaurant]], a page describing food source policies. In the case of a [[NewsMediaOrganization]], an ethicsPolicy is typically a statement describing the personal, organizational, and corporate standards of behavior expected by the organization.

@graph.rdfs:label: runtimePlatform
@graph.name: runtimePlatform
@graph.rdfs:comment: Runtime platform or script interpreter dependencies (example: Java v1, Python 2.3, .NET Framework 3.0).

@graph.rdfs:label: eduQuestionType
@graph.name: eduQuestionType
@graph.rdfs:comment: For questions that are part of learning resources (e.g. Quiz), eduQuestionType indicates the format of question being given. Example: "Multiple choice", "Open ended", "Flashcard".

@graph.rdfs:label: associatedAnatomy
@graph.name: associatedAnatomy
@graph.rdfs:comment: The anatomy of the underlying organ system or structures associated with this entity.

@graph.rdfs:label: appliesToPaymentMethod
@graph.name: appliesToPaymentMethod
@graph.rdfs:comment: The payment method(s) to which the payment charge specification applies.

@graph.rdfs:label: dependencies
@graph.name: dependencies
@graph.rdfs:comment: Prerequisites needed to fulfill steps in article.

@graph.rdfs:label: BusinessFunction
@graph.name: BusinessFunction
@graph.rdfs:comment:
The business function specifies the type of activity or access (i.e., the bundle of rights) offered by the organization or business person through the offer. Typical are sell, rental or lease, maintenance or repair, manufacture / produce, recycle / dispose, engineering / construction, or installation. Proprietary specifications of access rights are also instances of this class.

Commonly used values:

* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#ConstructionInstallation
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Dispose
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#LeaseOut
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Maintain
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#ProvideService
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Repair
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Sell
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Buy

@graph.rdfs:label: dietFeatures
@graph.name: dietFeatures
@graph.rdfs:comment: Nutritional information specific to the dietary plan. May include dietary recommendations on what foods to avoid, what foods to consume, and specific alterations/deviations from the USDA or other regulatory body's approved dietary guidelines.

@graph.rdfs:label: ScholarlyArticle
@graph.name: ScholarlyArticle
@graph.rdfs:comment: A scholarly article.

@graph.rdfs:label: servicePostalAddress
@graph.name: servicePostalAddress
@graph.rdfs:comment: The address for accessing the service by mail.

@graph.rdfs:label: hasMerchantReturnPolicy
@graph.name: hasMerchantReturnPolicy
@graph.rdfs:comment: Specifies a MerchantReturnPolicy that may be applicable.

@graph.rdfs:label: isAvailableGenerically
@graph.name: isAvailableGenerically
@graph.rdfs:comment: True if the drug is available in a generic form (regardless of name).

@graph.rdfs:label: buyer
@graph.name: buyer
@graph.rdfs:comment: A sub property of participant. The participant/person/organization that bought the object.

@graph.rdfs:label: OpinionNewsArticle
@graph.name: OpinionNewsArticle
@graph.rdfs:comment: An [[OpinionNewsArticle]] is a [[NewsArticle]] that primarily expresses opinions rather than journalistic reporting of news and events. For example, a [[NewsArticle]] consisting of a column or [[Blog]]/[[BlogPosting]] entry in the Opinions section of a news publication.

@graph.rdfs:label: sugarContent
@graph.name: sugarContent
@graph.rdfs:comment: The number of grams of sugar.

@graph.rdfs:label: howPerformed
@graph.name: howPerformed
@graph.rdfs:comment: How the procedure is performed.

@graph.rdfs:label: awards
@graph.name: awards
@graph.rdfs:comment: Awards won by or for this item.

@graph.rdfs:label: flightDistance
@graph.name: flightDistance
@graph.rdfs:comment: The distance of the flight.

@graph.rdfs:label: countryOfLastProcessing
@graph.name: countryOfLastProcessing
@graph.rdfs:comment: The place where the item (typically [[Product]]) was last processed and tested before importation.

@graph.rdfs:label: upvoteCount
@graph.name: upvoteCount
@graph.rdfs:comment: The number of upvotes this question, answer or comment has received from the community.

@graph.rdfs:label: customer
@graph.name: customer
@graph.rdfs:comment: Party placing the order or paying the invoice.

@graph.rdfs:label: ReplaceAction
@graph.name: ReplaceAction
@graph.rdfs:comment: The act of editing a recipient by replacing an old object with a new object.

@graph.rdfs:label: polygon
@graph.name: polygon
@graph.rdfs:comment: A polygon is the area enclosed by a point-to-point path for which the starting and ending points are the same. A polygon is expressed as a series of four or more space delimited points where the first and final points are identical.

@graph.rdfs:label: missionCoveragePrioritiesPolicy
@graph.name: missionCoveragePrioritiesPolicy
@graph.rdfs:comment: For a [[NewsMediaOrganization]], a statement on coverage priorities, including any public agenda or stance on issues.

@graph.rdfs:label: vehicleEngine
@graph.name: vehicleEngine
@graph.rdfs:comment: Information about the engine or engines of the vehicle.

@graph.rdfs:label: exercisePlan
@graph.name: exercisePlan
@graph.rdfs:comment: A sub property of instrument. The exercise plan used on this action.

@graph.rdfs:label: mealService
@graph.name: mealService
@graph.rdfs:comment: Description of the meals that will be provided or available for purchase.

@graph.rdfs:label: DateTime
@graph.name: DateTime
@graph.rdfs:comment: A combination of date and time of day in the form [-]CCYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss[Z|(+|-)hh:mm] (see Chapter 5.4 of ISO 8601).

@graph.rdfs:label: DigitalDocument
@graph.name: DigitalDocument
@graph.rdfs:comment: An electronic file or document.

@graph.rdfs:label: performers
@graph.name: performers
@graph.rdfs:comment: The main performer or performers of the event—for example, a presenter, musician, or actor.

@graph.rdfs:label: SkiResort
@graph.name: SkiResort
@graph.rdfs:comment: A ski resort.

@graph.rdfs:label: EventReservation
@graph.name: EventReservation
@graph.rdfs:comment: A reservation for an event like a concert, sporting event, or lecture.\n\nNote: This type is for information about actual reservations, e.g. in confirmation emails or HTML pages with individual confirmations of reservations. For offers of tickets, use [[Offer]].

@graph.rdfs:label: SuspendAction
@graph.name: SuspendAction
@graph.rdfs:comment: The act of momentarily pausing a device or application (e.g. pause music playback or pause a timer).

@graph.rdfs:label: runtime
@graph.name: runtime
@graph.rdfs:comment: Runtime platform or script interpreter dependencies (example: Java v1, Python 2.3, .NET Framework 3.0).

@graph.rdfs:label: urlTemplate
@graph.name: urlTemplate
@graph.rdfs:comment: An url template (RFC6570) that will be used to construct the target of the execution of the action.

@graph.rdfs:label: ProfessionalService
@graph.name: ProfessionalService
@graph.rdfs:comment:
Original definition: "provider of professional services."\n\nThe general [[ProfessionalService]] type for local businesses was deprecated due to confusion with [[Service]]. For reference, the types that it included were: [[Dentist]],
        [[AccountingService]], [[Attorney]], [[Notary]], as well as types for several kinds of [[HomeAndConstructionBusiness]]: [[Electrician]], [[GeneralContractor]],
        [[HousePainter]], [[Locksmith]], [[Plumber]], [[RoofingContractor]]. [[LegalService]] was introduced as a more inclusive supertype of [[Attorney]].

@graph.rdfs:label: acquiredFrom
@graph.name: acquiredFrom
@graph.rdfs:comment: The organization or person from which the product was acquired.

@graph.rdfs:label: drainsTo
@graph.name: drainsTo
@graph.rdfs:comment: The vasculature that the vein drains into.

@graph.rdfs:label: OfferItemCondition
@graph.name: OfferItemCondition
@graph.rdfs:comment: A list of possible conditions for the item.

@graph.rdfs:label: EntertainmentBusiness
@graph.name: EntertainmentBusiness
@graph.rdfs:comment: A business providing entertainment.

@graph.rdfs:label: cvdNumC19HospPats
@graph.name: cvdNumC19HospPats
@graph.rdfs:comment: numc19hosppats - HOSPITALIZED: Patients currently hospitalized in an inpatient care location who have suspected or confirmed COVID-19.

@graph.rdfs:label: publicTransportClosuresInfo
@graph.name: publicTransportClosuresInfo

@graph.rdfs:label: application
@graph.name: application
@graph.rdfs:comment: An application that can complete the request.

@graph.rdfs:label: feesAndCommissionsSpecification
@graph.name: feesAndCommissionsSpecification
@graph.rdfs:comment: Description of fees, commissions, and other terms applied either to a class of financial product, or by a financial service organization.

@graph.rdfs:label: WPFooter
@graph.name: WPFooter
@graph.rdfs:comment: The footer section of the page.

@graph.rdfs:label: RsvpResponseType
@graph.name: RsvpResponseType

@graph.rdfs:label: Volcano
@graph.name: Volcano
@graph.rdfs:comment: A volcano, like Fujisan.

@graph.rdfs:label: ApartmentComplex
@graph.name: ApartmentComplex
@graph.rdfs:comment: Residence type: Apartment complex.

@graph.rdfs:label: MedicalProcedureType
@graph.name: MedicalProcedureType
@graph.rdfs:comment: An enumeration that describes different types of medical procedures.

@graph.rdfs:label: ItemPage
@graph.name: ItemPage
@graph.rdfs:comment: A page devoted to a single item, such as a particular product or hotel.

@graph.rdfs:label: TransferAction
@graph.name: TransferAction
@graph.rdfs:comment: The act of transferring/moving (abstract or concrete) animate or inanimate objects from one place to another.

@graph.rdfs:label: billingIncrement
@graph.name: billingIncrement
@graph.rdfs:comment: This property specifies the minimal quantity and rounding increment that will be the basis for the billing. The unit of measurement is specified by the unitCode property.

@graph.rdfs:label: MotorcycleDealer
@graph.name: MotorcycleDealer

@graph.rdfs:label: bodyType
@graph.name: bodyType

@graph.rdfs:label: Joint

@graph.rdfs:comment: The anatomical location at which two or more bones make contact.

@graph.rdfs:label: Date
@graph.name: Date
@graph.rdfs:comment: A date value in [ISO 8601 date format](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601).

@graph.rdfs:label: seriousAdverseOutcome
@graph.name: seriousAdverseOutcome
@graph.rdfs:comment: A possible serious complication and/or serious side effect of this therapy. Serious adverse outcomes include those that are life-threatening; result in death, disability, or permanent damage; require hospitalization or prolong existing hospitalization; cause congenital anomalies or birth defects; or jeopardize the patient and may require medical or surgical intervention to prevent one of the outcomes in this definition.

@graph.rdfs:label: DigitalDocumentPermission
@graph.name: DigitalDocumentPermission
@graph.rdfs:comment: A permission for a particular person or group to access a particular file.

@graph.rdfs:label: RadioSeries
@graph.name: RadioSeries
@graph.rdfs:comment: CreativeWorkSeries dedicated to radio broadcast and associated online delivery.

@graph.rdfs:label: productID
@graph.name: productID
@graph.rdfs:comment: The product identifier, such as ISBN. For example: ``` meta itemprop="productID" content="isbn:123-456-789" ```.

@graph.rdfs:label: NonprofitType
@graph.name: NonprofitType
@graph.rdfs:comment: NonprofitType enumerates several kinds of official non-profit types of which a non-profit organization can be.

@graph.rdfs:label: AggregateOffer
@graph.name: AggregateOffer
@graph.rdfs:comment: When a single product is associated with multiple offers (for example, the same pair of shoes is offered by different merchants), then AggregateOffer can be used.\n\nNote: AggregateOffers are normally expected to associate multiple offers that all share the same defined [[businessFunction]] value, or default to http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Sell if businessFunction is not explicitly defined.

@graph.name: interactionStatistic
@graph.rdfs:comment: The number of interactions for the CreativeWork using the WebSite or SoftwareApplication. The most specific child type of InteractionCounter should be used.

@graph.rdfs:label: TherapeuticProcedure
@graph.name: TherapeuticProcedure
@graph.rdfs:comment: A medical procedure intended primarily for therapeutic purposes, aimed at improving a health condition.

@graph.rdfs:label: jobStartDate
@graph.name: jobStartDate
@graph.rdfs:comment: The date on which a successful applicant for this job would be expected to start work. Choose a specific date in the future or use the jobImmediateStart property to indicate the position is to be filled as soon as possible.

@graph.rdfs:label: estimatedSalary
@graph.name: estimatedSalary
@graph.rdfs:comment: An estimated salary for a job posting or occupation, based on a variety of variables including, but not limited to industry, job title, and location. Estimated salaries  are often computed by outside organizations rather than the hiring organization, who may not have committed to the estimated value.

@graph.rdfs:label: employees
@graph.name: employees
@graph.rdfs:comment: People working for this organization.

@graph.rdfs:label: Crematorium
@graph.name: Crematorium
@graph.rdfs:comment: A crematorium.

@graph.rdfs:label: targetPlatform
@graph.name: targetPlatform
@graph.rdfs:comment: Type of app development: phone, Metro style, desktop, XBox, etc.

@graph.rdfs:label: geo
@graph.name: geo
@graph.rdfs:comment: The geo coordinates of the place.

@graph.rdfs:label: recipeIngredient
@graph.name: recipeIngredient
@graph.rdfs:comment: An ingredient or ordered list of ingredients and potentially quantities used in the recipe, e.g. 1 cup of sugar, flour or garlic.  The ingredients can be represented as free text or more structured values.

@graph.rdfs:label: TheaterGroup
@graph.name: TheaterGroup
@graph.rdfs:comment: A theater group or company, for example, the Royal Shakespeare Company or Druid Theatre.

@graph.rdfs:label: assemblyVersion
@graph.name: assemblyVersion
@graph.rdfs:comment: Associated product/technology version. E.g., .NET Framework 4.5.

@graph.rdfs:label: contentUrl
@graph.name: contentUrl
@graph.rdfs:comment: Actual bytes of the media object, for example the image file or video file.

@graph.rdfs:label: supply
@graph.name: supply
@graph.rdfs:comment: A sub-property of instrument. A supply consumed when performing instructions or a direction.

@graph.rdfs:label: source
@graph.name: source
@graph.rdfs:comment: The source or cause of the event.

@graph.rdfs:label: recommendationStrength
@graph.name: recommendationStrength
@graph.rdfs:comment: Strength of the guideline's recommendation (e.g. 'class I').

@graph.rdfs:label: geoTouches
@graph.name: geoTouches
@graph.rdfs:comment: Represents spatial relations in which two geometries (or the places they represent) touch: "they have at least one boundary point in common, but no interior points." (A symmetric relationship, as defined in [DE-9IM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DE-9IM).)

@graph.rdfs:label: fundedItem
@graph.name: fundedItem
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indicates something directly or indirectly funded or sponsored through a [[Grant]]. See also [[ownershipFundingInfo]].

@graph.rdfs:label: postOfficeBoxNumber
@graph.name: postOfficeBoxNumber
@graph.rdfs:comment: The post office box number for PO box addresses.

@graph.rdfs:label: MusicRelease
@graph.name: MusicRelease
@graph.rdfs:comment: A MusicRelease is a specific release of a music album.

@graph.rdfs:label: SpecialAnnouncement
@graph.name: SpecialAnnouncement
@graph.rdfs:comment:
A SpecialAnnouncement combines a simple date-stamped textual information update
      with contextualized Web links and other structured data.  It represents an information update made by a
      locally-oriented organization, for example schools, pharmacies, healthcare providers,  community groups, police,
      local government.

For work in progress guidelines on Coronavirus-related markup see [this doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14ikaGCKxo50rRM7nvKSlbUpjyIk2WMQd3IkB1lItlrM/edit#).

The motivating scenario for SpecialAnnouncement is the [Coronavirus pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_coronavirus_pandemic), and the initial vocabulary is oriented to this urgent situation. Schema.org
expect to improve the markup iteratively as it is deployed and as feedback emerges from use. In addition to our
usual [Github entry](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/2490), feedback comments can also be provided in [this document](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fpdFFxk8s87CWwACs53SGkYv3aafSxz_DTtOQxMrBJQ/edit#).


While this schema is designed to communicate urgent crisis-related information, it is not the same as an emergency warning technology like [CAP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_Alerting_Protocol), although there may be overlaps. The intent is to cover
the kinds of everyday practical information being posted to existing websites during an emergency situation.

Several kinds of information can be provided:

We encourage the provision of "name", "text", "datePosted", "expires" (if appropriate), "category" and
"url" as a simple baseline. It is important to provide a value for "category" where possible, most ideally as a well known
URL from Wikipedia or Wikidata. In the case of the 2019-2020 Coronavirus pandemic, this should be "https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2019-20\_coronavirus\_pandemic" or "https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q81068910".

For many of the possible properties, values can either be simple links or an inline description, depending on whether a summary is available. For a link, provide just the URL of the appropriate page as the property's value. For an inline description, use a [[WebContent]] type, and provide the url as a property of that, alongside at least a simple "[[text]]" summary of the page. It is
unlikely that a single SpecialAnnouncement will need all of the possible properties simultaneously.

We expect that in many cases the page referenced might contain more specialized structured data, e.g. contact info, [[openingHours]], [[Event]], [[FAQPage]] etc. By linking to those pages from a [[SpecialAnnouncement]] you can help make it clearer that the events are related to the situation (e.g. Coronavirus) indicated by the [[category]] property of the [[SpecialAnnouncement]].

Many [[SpecialAnnouncement]]s will relate to particular regions and to identifiable local organizations. Use [[spatialCoverage]] for the region, and [[announcementLocation]] to indicate specific [[LocalBusiness]]es and [[CivicStructure]]s. If the announcement affects both a particular region and a specific location (for example, a library closure that serves an entire region), use both [[spatialCoverage]] and [[announcementLocation]].

The [[about]] property can be used to indicate entities that are the focus of the announcement. We now recommend using [[about]] only
for representing non-location entities (e.g. a [[Course]] or a [[RadioStation]]). For places, use [[announcementLocation]] and [[spatialCoverage]]. Consumers of this markup should be aware that the initial design encouraged the use of [[about]] for locations too.

The basic content of [[SpecialAnnouncement]] is similar to that of an [RSS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RSS) or [Atom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atom_(Web_standard)) feed. For publishers without such feeds, basic feed-like information can be shared by posting
[[SpecialAnnouncement]] updates in a page, e.g. using JSON-LD. For sites with Atom/RSS functionality, you can point to a feed
with the [[webFeed]] property. This can be a simple URL, or an inline [[DataFeed]] object, with [[encodingFormat]] providing
media type information, e.g. "application/rss+xml" or "application/atom+xml".

@graph.rdfs:label: jobTitle
@graph.name: jobTitle
@graph.rdfs:comment: The job title of the person (for example, Financial Manager).

@graph.rdfs:label: associatedPathophysiology
@graph.name: associatedPathophysiology
@graph.rdfs:comment: If applicable, a description of the pathophysiology associated with the anatomical system, including potential abnormal changes in the mechanical, physical, and biochemical functions of the system.

@graph.rdfs:label: endorsers
@graph.name: endorsers
@graph.rdfs:comment: People or organizations that endorse the plan.

@graph.rdfs:label: OrganizeAction
@graph.name: OrganizeAction
@graph.rdfs:comment: The act of manipulating/administering/supervising/controlling one or more objects.

@graph.rdfs:label: Periodical
@graph.name: Periodical
@graph.rdfs:comment: A publication in any medium issued in successive parts bearing numerical or chronological designations and intended to continue indefinitely, such as a magazine, scholarly journal, or newspaper.\n\nSee also [blog post](https://blog.schema.org/2014/09/02/schema-org-support-for-bibliographic-relationships-and-periodicals/).

@graph.rdfs:label: educationRequirements
@graph.name: educationRequirements
@graph.rdfs:comment: Educational background needed for the position or Occupation.

@graph.rdfs:label: cargoVolume
@graph.name: cargoVolume
@graph.rdfs:comment:
The available volume for cargo or luggage. For automobiles, this is usually the trunk volume.

Typical unit code(s): LTR for liters, FTQ for cubic foot/feet

Note: You can use [[minValue]] and [[maxValue]] to indicate ranges.

@graph.rdfs:label: SocialMediaPosting
@graph.name: SocialMediaPosting
@graph.rdfs:comment: A post to a social media platform, including blog posts, tweets, Facebook posts, etc.

@graph.rdfs:label: headline
@graph.name: headline
@graph.rdfs:comment: Headline of the article.

@graph.rdfs:label: primaryPrevention
@graph.name: primaryPrevention
@graph.rdfs:comment: A preventative therapy used to prevent an initial occurrence of the medical condition, such as vaccination.

@graph.rdfs:label: blogPost
@graph.name: blogPost
@graph.rdfs:comment: A posting that is part of this blog.

@graph.rdfs:label: exceptDate
@graph.name: exceptDate
@graph.rdfs:comment:
Defines a [[Date]] or [[DateTime]] during which a scheduled [[Event]] will not take place. The property allows exceptions to
      a [[Schedule]] to be specified. If an exception is specified as a [[DateTime]] then only the event that would have started at that specific date and time
      should be excluded from the schedule. If an exception is specified as a [[Date]] then any event that is scheduled for that 24 hour period should be
      excluded from the schedule. This allows a whole day to be excluded from the schedule without having to itemise every scheduled event.

@graph.rdfs:label: fuelCapacity
@graph.name: fuelCapacity
@graph.rdfs:comment: The capacity of the fuel tank or in the case of electric cars, the battery. If there are multiple components for storage, this should indicate the total of all storage of the same type.\n\nTypical unit code(s): LTR for liters, GLL of US gallons, GLI for UK / imperial gallons, AMH for ampere-hours (for electrical vehicles).

@graph.rdfs:label: cvdNumBeds
@graph.name: cvdNumBeds
@graph.rdfs:comment: numbeds - HOSPITAL INPATIENT BEDS: Inpatient beds, including all staffed, licensed, and overflow (surge) beds used for inpatients.

@graph.rdfs:label: TattooParlor
@graph.name: TattooParlor
@graph.rdfs:comment: A tattoo parlor.

@graph.rdfs:label: ClothingStore
@graph.name: ClothingStore
@graph.rdfs:comment: A clothing store.

@graph.rdfs:label: emissionsCO2
@graph.name: emissionsCO2
@graph.rdfs:comment: The CO2 emissions in g/km. When used in combination with a QuantitativeValue, put "g/km" into the unitText property of that value, since there is no UN/CEFACT Common Code for "g/km".

@graph.rdfs:label: Guide
@graph.name: Guide
@graph.rdfs:comment: [[Guide]] is a page or article that recommends specific products or services, or aspects of a thing for a user to consider. A [[Guide]] may represent a Buying Guide and detail aspects of products or services for a user to consider. A [[Guide]] may represent a Product Guide and recommend specific products or services. A [[Guide]] may represent a Ranked List and recommend specific products or services with ranking.

@graph.rdfs:label: MoveAction
@graph.name: MoveAction
@graph.rdfs:comment:
The act of an agent relocating to a place.

Related actions:

* [[TransferAction]]: Unlike TransferAction, the subject of the move is a living Person or Organization rather than an inanimate object.

@graph.rdfs:label: MiddleSchool
@graph.name: MiddleSchool
@graph.rdfs:comment: A middle school (typically for children aged around 11-14, although this varies somewhat).

@graph.rdfs:label: MovieSeries
@graph.name: MovieSeries
@graph.rdfs:comment: A series of movies. Included movies can be indicated with the hasPart property.

@graph.rdfs:label: priceCurrency
@graph.name: priceCurrency
@graph.rdfs:comment: The currency of the price, or a price component when attached to [[PriceSpecification]] and its subtypes.\n\nUse standard formats: [ISO 4217 currency format](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217), e.g. "USD"; [Ticker symbol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cryptocurrencies) for cryptocurrencies, e.g. "BTC"; well known names for [Local Exchange Trading Systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_exchange_trading_system) (LETS) and other currency types, e.g. "Ithaca HOUR".

@graph.rdfs:label: mainEntity
@graph.name: mainEntity
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indicates the primary entity described in some page or other CreativeWork.

@graph.rdfs:label: experienceInPlaceOfEducation
@graph.name: experienceInPlaceOfEducation
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indicates whether a [[JobPosting]] will accept experience (as indicated by [[OccupationalExperienceRequirements]]) in place of its formal educational qualifications (as indicated by [[educationRequirements]]). If true, indicates that satisfying one of these requirements is sufficient.

@graph.rdfs:label: eligibleRegion
@graph.name: eligibleRegion
@graph.rdfs:comment: The ISO 3166-1 (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) or ISO 3166-2 code, the place, or the GeoShape for the geo-political region(s) for which the offer or delivery charge specification is valid.\n\nSee also [[ineligibleRegion]].

@graph.rdfs:label: DownloadAction
@graph.name: DownloadAction
@graph.rdfs:comment: The act of downloading an object.

@graph.rdfs:label: relatedTo
@graph.name: relatedTo
@graph.rdfs:comment: The most generic familial relation.

@graph.rdfs:label: jurisdiction
@graph.name: jurisdiction
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indicates a legal jurisdiction, e.g. of some legislation, or where some government service is based.

@graph.rdfs:label: TradeAction
@graph.name: TradeAction
@graph.rdfs:comment: The act of participating in an exchange of goods and services for monetary compensation. An agent trades an object, product or service with a participant in exchange for a one time or periodic payment.

@graph.rdfs:label: purchaseDate
@graph.name: purchaseDate
@graph.rdfs:comment: The date the item, e.g. vehicle, was purchased by the current owner.

@graph.rdfs:label: founder
@graph.name: founder
@graph.rdfs:comment: A person or organization who founded this organization.

@graph.rdfs:label: Table
@graph.name: Table
@graph.rdfs:comment: A table on a Web page.

@graph.rdfs:label: timeOfDay
@graph.name: timeOfDay
@graph.rdfs:comment: The time of day the program normally runs. For example, "evenings".

@graph.rdfs:label: ContactPointOption
@graph.name: ContactPointOption
@graph.rdfs:comment: Enumerated options related to a ContactPoint.

@graph.rdfs:label: returnPolicyCategory
@graph.name: returnPolicyCategory
@graph.rdfs:comment: Specifies an applicable return policy (from an enumeration).

@graph.rdfs:label: spouse
@graph.name: spouse
@graph.rdfs:comment: The person's spouse.

@graph.rdfs:label: copyrightHolder
@graph.name: copyrightHolder
@graph.rdfs:comment: The party holding the legal copyright to the CreativeWork.

@graph.rdfs:label: agent
@graph.name: agent
@graph.rdfs:comment: The direct performer or driver of the action (animate or inanimate). E.g. *John* wrote a book.

@graph.rdfs:label: customerRemorseReturnLabelSource
@graph.name: customerRemorseReturnLabelSource
@graph.rdfs:comment: The method (from an enumeration) by which the customer obtains a return shipping label for a product returned due to customer remorse.

@graph.rdfs:label: busNumber
@graph.name: busNumber
@graph.rdfs:comment: The unique identifier for the bus.

@graph.rdfs:label: foodEvent
@graph.name: foodEvent
@graph.rdfs:comment: A sub property of location. The specific food event where the action occurred.

@graph.rdfs:label: BroadcastChannel
@graph.name: BroadcastChannel
@graph.rdfs:comment: A unique instance of a BroadcastService on a CableOrSatelliteService lineup.

@graph.rdfs:label: homeTeam
@graph.name: homeTeam
@graph.rdfs:comment: The home team in a sports event.

@graph.rdfs:label: greater
@graph.name: greater
@graph.rdfs:comment: This ordering relation for qualitative values indicates that the subject is greater than the object.

@graph.rdfs:label: PaymentMethodType
@graph.name: PaymentMethodType
@graph.rdfs:comment: The type of payment method, only for generic payment types, specific forms of payments, like card payment should be expressed using subclasses of PaymentMethod.

@graph.rdfs:label: gracePeriod
@graph.name: gracePeriod
@graph.rdfs:comment: The period of time after any due date that the borrower has to fulfil its obligations before a default (failure to pay) is deemed to have occurred.

@graph.rdfs:label: itemDefectReturnShippingFeesAmount
@graph.name: itemDefectReturnShippingFeesAmount
@graph.rdfs:comment: Amount of shipping costs for defect product returns. Applicable when property [[itemDefectReturnFees]] equals [[ReturnShippingFees]].

@graph.rdfs:label: digitalSourceType
@graph.name: digitalSourceType
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indicates an IPTCDigitalSourceEnumeration code indicating the nature of the digital source(s) for some [[CreativeWork]].

@graph.rdfs:label: teaches
@graph.name: teaches
@graph.rdfs:comment: The item being described is intended to help a person learn the competency or learning outcome defined by the referenced term.

@graph.rdfs:label: Casino
@graph.name: Casino
@graph.rdfs:comment: A casino.

@graph.rdfs:label: ServicePeriod
@graph.name: ServicePeriod
@graph.rdfs:comment: ServicePeriod represents a duration with some constraints about cutoff time and business days. This is used e.g. in shipping for handling times or transit time.

@graph.rdfs:label: PalliativeProcedure
@graph.name: PalliativeProcedure
@graph.rdfs:comment: A medical procedure intended primarily for palliative purposes, aimed at relieving the symptoms of an underlying health condition.

@graph.rdfs:label: coach
@graph.name: coach
@graph.rdfs:comment: A person that acts in a coaching role for a sports team.

@graph.rdfs:label: Plumber
@graph.name: Plumber
@graph.rdfs:comment: A plumbing service.

@graph.rdfs:label: VideoGameClip
@graph.name: VideoGameClip
@graph.rdfs:comment: A short segment/part of a video game.

@graph.rdfs:label: bookEdition
@graph.name: bookEdition
@graph.rdfs:comment: The edition of the book.

@graph.rdfs:label: version
@graph.name: version
@graph.rdfs:comment: The version of the CreativeWork embodied by a specified resource.

@graph.rdfs:label: amenityFeature
@graph.name: amenityFeature
@graph.rdfs:comment: An amenity feature (e.g. a characteristic or service) of the Accommodation. This generic property does not make a statement about whether the feature is included in an offer for the main accommodation or available at extra costs.

@graph.rdfs:label: temporalCoverage
@graph.name: temporalCoverage
@graph.rdfs:comment:
The temporalCoverage of a CreativeWork indicates the period that the content applies to, i.e. that it describes, either as a DateTime or as a textual string indicating a time period in [ISO 8601 time interval format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601#Time_intervals). In
      the case of a Dataset it will typically indicate the relevant time period in a precise notation (e.g. for a 2011 census dataset, the year 2011 would be written "2011/2012"). Other forms of content, e.g. ScholarlyArticle, Book, TVSeries or TVEpisode, may indicate their temporalCoverage in broader terms - textually or via well-known URL.
      Written works such as books may sometimes have precise temporal coverage too, e.g. a work set in 1939 - 1945 can be indicated in ISO 8601 interval format format via "1939/1945".

Open-ended date ranges can be written with ".." in place of the end date. For example, "2015-11/.." indicates a range beginning in November 2015 and with no specified final date. This is tentative and might be updated in future when ISO 8601 is officially updated.

@graph.rdfs:label: Organization
@graph.name: Organization
@graph.rdfs:comment: An organization such as a school, NGO, corporation, club, etc.

@graph.rdfs:label: MedicalAudienceType
@graph.name: MedicalAudienceType
@graph.rdfs:comment: Target audiences types for medical web pages. Enumerated type.

@graph.rdfs:label: pageEnd
@graph.name: pageEnd
@graph.rdfs:comment: The page on which the work ends; for example "138" or "xvi".

@graph.rdfs:label: eligibleTransactionVolume
@graph.name: eligibleTransactionVolume
@graph.rdfs:comment: The transaction volume, in a monetary unit, for which the offer or price specification is valid, e.g. for indicating a minimal purchasing volume, to express free shipping above a certain order volume, or to limit the acceptance of credit cards to purchases to a certain minimal amount.

@graph.rdfs:label: BikeStore
@graph.name: BikeStore
@graph.rdfs:comment: A bike store.

@graph.rdfs:label: free
@graph.name: free
@graph.rdfs:comment: A flag to signal that the item, event, or place is accessible for free.

@graph.rdfs:label: LocationFeatureSpecification
@graph.name: LocationFeatureSpecification
@graph.rdfs:comment: Specifies a location feature by providing a structured value representing a feature of an accommodation as a property-value pair of varying degrees of formality.

@graph.rdfs:label: streetAddress
@graph.name: streetAddress
@graph.rdfs:comment: The street address. For example, 1600 Amphitheatre Pkwy.

@graph.rdfs:label: cvdFacilityCounty
@graph.name: cvdFacilityCounty
@graph.rdfs:comment: Name of the County of the NHSN facility that this data record applies to. Use [[cvdFacilityId]] to identify the facility. To provide other details, [[healthcareReportingData]] can be used on a [[Hospital]] entry.

@graph.rdfs:label: accessModeSufficient
@graph.name: accessModeSufficient
@graph.rdfs:comment: A list of single or combined access modes that are sufficient to understand all the intellectual content of a resource, including any adaptations. Values should be drawn from the [approved vocabulary](https://www.w3.org/2021/a11y-discov-vocab/latest/#accessModeSufficient-vocabulary).

@graph.rdfs:label: printSection
@graph.name: printSection
@graph.rdfs:comment: If this NewsArticle appears in print, this field indicates the print section in which the article appeared.

@graph.rdfs:label: WarrantyPromise
@graph.name: WarrantyPromise
@graph.rdfs:comment: A structured value representing the duration and scope of services that will be provided to a customer free of charge in case of a defect or malfunction of a product.

@graph.rdfs:label: hasMap
@graph.name: hasMap
@graph.rdfs:comment: A URL to a map of the place.

@graph.rdfs:label: lyrics
@graph.name: lyrics
@graph.rdfs:comment: The words in the song.

@graph.rdfs:label: CampingPitch
@graph.name: CampingPitch
@graph.rdfs:comment:
A [[CampingPitch]] is an individual place for overnight stay in the outdoors, typically being part of a larger camping site, or [[Campground]].\n\n
In British English a campsite, or campground, is an area, usually divided into a number of pitches, where people can camp overnight using tents or camper vans or caravans; this British English use of the word is synonymous with the American English expression campground. In American English the term campsite generally means an area where an individual, family, group, or military unit can pitch a tent or park a camper; a campground may contain many campsites.
(Source: Wikipedia, see [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campsite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campsite).)\n\n
See also the dedicated [document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations](/docs/hotels.html).

@graph.rdfs:label: clinicalPharmacology
@graph.name: clinicalPharmacology
@graph.rdfs:comment: Description of the absorption and elimination of drugs, including their concentration (pharmacokinetics, pK) and biological effects (pharmacodynamics, pD).

@graph.rdfs:label: ccRecipient
@graph.name: ccRecipient
@graph.rdfs:comment: A sub property of recipient. The recipient copied on a message.

@graph.rdfs:label: directors
@graph.name: directors
@graph.rdfs:comment: A director of e.g. TV, radio, movie, video games etc. content. Directors can be associated with individual items or with a series, episode, clip.

@graph.rdfs:label: OpeningHoursSpecification
@graph.name: OpeningHoursSpecification
@graph.rdfs:comment:
A structured value providing information about the opening hours of a place or a certain service inside a place.


The place is __open__ if the [[opens]] property is specified, and __closed__ otherwise.

If the value for the [[closes]] property is less than the value for the [[opens]] property then the hour range is assumed to span over the next day.

@graph.rdfs:label: HyperTocEntry
@graph.name: HyperTocEntry
@graph.rdfs:comment: A HyperToEntry is an item within a [[HyperToc]], which represents a hypertext table of contents for complex media objects, such as [[VideoObject]], [[AudioObject]]. The media object itself is indicated using [[associatedMedia]]. Each section of interest within that content can be described with a [[HyperTocEntry]], with associated [[startOffset]] and [[endOffset]]. When several entries are all from the same file, [[associatedMedia]] is used on the overarching [[HyperTocEntry]]; if the content has been split into multiple files, they can be referenced using [[associatedMedia]] on each [[HyperTocEntry]].

@graph.rdfs:label: arrivalStation
@graph.name: arrivalStation
@graph.rdfs:comment: The station where the train trip ends.

@graph.rdfs:label: accessibilityFeature
@graph.name: accessibilityFeature
@graph.rdfs:comment: Content features of the resource, such as accessible media, alternatives and supported enhancements for accessibility. Values should be drawn from the [approved vocabulary](https://www.w3.org/2021/a11y-discov-vocab/latest/#accessibilityFeature-vocabulary).

@graph.rdfs:label: ratingCount
@graph.name: ratingCount
@graph.rdfs:comment: The count of total number of ratings.

@graph.rdfs:label: valueRequired
@graph.name: valueRequired
@graph.rdfs:comment: Whether the property must be filled in to complete the action.  Default is false.

@graph.rdfs:label: DefinedRegion
@graph.name: DefinedRegion
@graph.rdfs:comment:
A DefinedRegion is a geographic area defined by potentially arbitrary (rather than political, administrative or natural geographical) criteria. Properties are provided for defining a region by reference to sets of postal codes.

Examples: a delivery destination when shopping. Region where regional pricing is configured.

Requirement 1:
Country: US
States: "NY", "CA"

Requirement 2:
Country: US
PostalCode Set: { [94000-94585], [97000, 97999], [13000, 13599]}
{ [12345, 12345], [78945, 78945], }
Region = state, canton, prefecture, autonomous community...

@graph.rdfs:label: numTracks
@graph.name: numTracks
@graph.rdfs:comment: The number of tracks in this album or playlist.

@graph.rdfs:label: screenCount
@graph.name: screenCount
@graph.rdfs:comment: The number of screens in the movie theater.

@graph.rdfs:label: DisagreeAction
@graph.name: DisagreeAction
@graph.rdfs:comment: The act of expressing a difference of opinion with the object. An agent disagrees to/about an object (a proposition, topic or theme) with participants.

@graph.rdfs:label: LymphaticVessel
@graph.name: LymphaticVessel
@graph.rdfs:comment: A type of blood vessel that specifically carries lymph fluid unidirectionally toward the heart.

@graph.rdfs:label: CompleteDataFeed
@graph.name: CompleteDataFeed
@graph.rdfs:comment:
A [[CompleteDataFeed]] is a [[DataFeed]] whose standard representation includes content for every item currently in the feed.

This is the equivalent of Atom's element as defined in Feed Paging and Archiving [RFC 5005](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5005), for example (and as defined for Atom), when using data from a feed that represents a collection of items that varies over time (e.g. "Top Twenty Records") there is no need to have newer entries mixed in alongside older, obsolete entries. By marking this feed as a CompleteDataFeed, old entries can be safely discarded when the feed is refreshed, since we can assume the feed has provided descriptions for all current items.

@graph.rdfs:label: Schedule
@graph.name: Schedule
@graph.rdfs:comment:
A schedule defines a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring [[Event]]. At a minimum a schedule will specify [[repeatFrequency]] which describes the interval between occurrences of the event. Additional information can be provided to specify the schedule more precisely.
      This includes identifying the day(s) of the week or month when the recurring event will take place, in addition to its start and end time. Schedules may also
      have start and end dates to indicate when they are active, e.g. to define a limited calendar of events.

@graph.rdfs:label: ArtGallery
@graph.name: ArtGallery
@graph.rdfs:comment: An art gallery.

@graph.rdfs:label: WebContent
@graph.name: WebContent
@graph.rdfs:comment: WebContent is a type representing all [[WebPage]], [[WebSite]] and [[WebPageElement]] content. It is sometimes the case that detailed distinctions between Web pages, sites and their parts are not always important or obvious. The  [[WebContent]] type makes it easier to describe Web-addressable content without requiring such distinctions to always be stated. (The intent is that the existing types [[WebPage]], [[WebSite]] and [[WebPageElement]] will eventually be declared as subtypes of [[WebContent]].)

@graph.rdfs:label: arterialBranch
@graph.name: arterialBranch
@graph.rdfs:comment: The branches that comprise the arterial structure.

@graph.rdfs:label: realEstateAgent
@graph.name: realEstateAgent
@graph.rdfs:comment: A sub property of participant. The real estate agent involved in the action.

@graph.rdfs:label: eventStatus
@graph.name: eventStatus
@graph.rdfs:comment: An eventStatus of an event represents its status; particularly useful when an event is cancelled or rescheduled.

@graph.rdfs:label: estimatedFlightDuration
@graph.name: estimatedFlightDuration
@graph.rdfs:comment: The estimated time the flight will take.

@graph.rdfs:label: remainingAttendeeCapacity
@graph.name: remainingAttendeeCapacity
@graph.rdfs:comment: The number of attendee places for an event that remain unallocated.

@graph.rdfs:label: RentAction
@graph.name: RentAction
@graph.rdfs:comment: The act of giving money in return for temporary use, but not ownership, of an object such as a vehicle or property. For example, an agent rents a property from a landlord in exchange for a periodic payment.

@graph.rdfs:label: ticketToken
@graph.name: ticketToken
@graph.rdfs:comment: Reference to an asset (e.g., Barcode, QR code image or PDF) usable for entrance.

@graph.rdfs:label: healthPlanPharmacyCategory
@graph.name: healthPlanPharmacyCategory
@graph.rdfs:comment: The category or type of pharmacy associated with this cost sharing.

@graph.rdfs:label: VitalSign
@graph.name: VitalSign
@graph.rdfs:comment: Vital signs are measures of various physiological functions in order to assess the most basic body functions.

@graph.rdfs:label: RentalCarReservation
@graph.name: RentalCarReservation
@graph.rdfs:comment: A reservation for a rental car.\n\nNote: This type is for information about actual reservations, e.g. in confirmation emails or HTML pages with individual confirmations of reservations.

@graph.rdfs:label: VideoGallery
@graph.name: VideoGallery
@graph.rdfs:comment: Web page type: Video gallery page.

@graph.rdfs:label: MobilePhoneStore
@graph.name: MobilePhoneStore
@graph.rdfs:comment: A store that sells mobile phones and related accessories.

@graph.rdfs:label: multipleValues
@graph.name: multipleValues
@graph.rdfs:comment: Whether multiple values are allowed for the property.  Default is false.

@graph.rdfs:label: defaultValue
@graph.name: defaultValue
@graph.rdfs:comment: The default value of the input.  For properties that expect a literal, the default is a literal value, for properties that expect an object, it's an ID reference to one of the current values.

@graph.rdfs:label: isAcceptingNewPatients
@graph.name: isAcceptingNewPatients
@graph.rdfs:comment: Whether the provider is accepting new patients.

@graph.rdfs:label: ConferenceEvent
@graph.name: ConferenceEvent
@graph.rdfs:comment: Event type: Conference event.

@graph.rdfs:label: DiscussionForumPosting
@graph.name: DiscussionForumPosting
@graph.rdfs:comment: A posting to a discussion forum.

@graph.rdfs:label: requiredMinAge
@graph.name: requiredMinAge
@graph.rdfs:comment: Audiences defined by a person's minimum age.

@graph.rdfs:label: EducationalOccupationalProgram
@graph.name: EducationalOccupationalProgram
@graph.rdfs:comment: A program offered by an institution which determines the learning progress to achieve an outcome, usually a credential like a degree or certificate. This would define a discrete set of opportunities (e.g., job, courses) that together constitute a program with a clear start, end, set of requirements, and transition to a new occupational opportunity (e.g., a job), or sometimes a higher educational opportunity (e.g., an advanced degree).

@graph.rdfs:label: InstantaneousEvent
@graph.name: InstantaneousEvent
@graph.rdfs:comment: An event with no duration, like for instance a computer log entry.

@graph.rdfs:label: cvdNumC19MechVentPats
@graph.name: cvdNumC19MechVentPats
@graph.rdfs:comment: numc19mechventpats - HOSPITALIZED and VENTILATED: Patients hospitalized in an NHSN inpatient care location who have suspected or confirmed COVID-19 and are on a mechanical ventilator.

@graph.rdfs:label: ElectronicsStore
@graph.name: ElectronicsStore
@graph.rdfs:comment: An electronics store.

@graph.rdfs:label: dayOfWeek
@graph.name: dayOfWeek
@graph.rdfs:comment: The day of the week for which these opening hours are valid.

@graph.rdfs:label: MedicalOrganization
@graph.name: MedicalOrganization
@graph.rdfs:comment: A medical organization (physical or not), such as hospital, institution or clinic.

@graph.rdfs:label: sizeGroup
@graph.name: sizeGroup
@graph.rdfs:comment: The size group (also known as "size type") for a product's size. Size groups are common in the fashion industry to define size segments and suggested audiences for wearable products. Multiple values can be combined, for example "men's big and tall", "petite maternity" or "regular".

@graph.rdfs:label: programPrerequisites
@graph.name: programPrerequisites
@graph.rdfs:comment: Prerequisites for enrolling in the program.

@graph.rdfs:label: CookAction
@graph.name: CookAction
@graph.rdfs:comment: The act of producing/preparing food.

@graph.rdfs:label: AgreeAction
@graph.name: AgreeAction
@graph.rdfs:comment: The act of expressing a consistency of opinion with the object. An agent agrees to/about an object (a proposition, topic or theme) with participants.

@graph.rdfs:label: departureBusStop
@graph.name: departureBusStop
@graph.rdfs:comment: The stop or station from which the bus departs.

@graph.rdfs:label: floorSize
@graph.name: floorSize
@graph.rdfs:comment:
The size of the accommodation, e.g. in square meter or squarefoot.
Typical unit code(s): MTK for square meter, FTK for square foot, or YDK for square yard.

@graph.rdfs:label: permissions
@graph.name: permissions
@graph.rdfs:comment: Permission(s) required to run the app (for example, a mobile app may require full internet access or may run only on wifi).

@graph.rdfs:label: inPlaylist
@graph.name: inPlaylist
@graph.rdfs:comment: The playlist to which this recording belongs.

@graph.rdfs:label: MedicalConditionStage
@graph.name: MedicalConditionStage
@graph.rdfs:comment: A stage of a medical condition, such as 'Stage IIIa'.

@graph.rdfs:label: gameAvailabilityType
@graph.name: gameAvailabilityType
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indicates the availability type of the game content associated with this action, such as whether it is a full version or a demo.

@graph.rdfs:label: workPerformed
@graph.name: workPerformed
@graph.rdfs:comment: A work performed in some event, for example a play performed in a TheaterEvent.

@graph.rdfs:label: floorLevel
@graph.name: floorLevel
@graph.rdfs:comment:
The floor level for an [[Accommodation]] in a multi-storey building. Since counting
  systems [vary internationally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storey#Consecutive_number_floor_designations), the local system should be used where possible.

@graph.rdfs:label: credentialCategory
@graph.name: credentialCategory
@graph.rdfs:comment: The category or type of credential being described, for example "degree”, “certificate”, “badge”, or more specific term.

@graph.rdfs:label: TrainTrip
@graph.name: TrainTrip
@graph.rdfs:comment: A trip on a commercial train line.

@graph.rdfs:label: recordedAs
@graph.name: recordedAs
@graph.rdfs:comment: An audio recording of the work.

@graph.rdfs:label: Festival
@graph.name: Festival
@graph.rdfs:comment: Event type: Festival.

@graph.rdfs:label: valuePattern
@graph.name: valuePattern
@graph.rdfs:comment: Specifies a regular expression for testing literal values according to the HTML spec.

@graph.rdfs:label: trackingNumber
@graph.name: trackingNumber
@graph.rdfs:comment: Shipper tracking number.

@graph.rdfs:label: ProductCollection
@graph.name: ProductCollection
@graph.rdfs:comment: A set of products (either [[ProductGroup]]s or specific variants) that are listed together e.g. in an [[Offer]].

@graph.rdfs:label: epidemiology
@graph.name: epidemiology
@graph.rdfs:comment: The characteristics of associated patients, such as age, gender, race etc.

@graph.rdfs:label: doseSchedule
@graph.name: doseSchedule
@graph.rdfs:comment: A dosing schedule for the drug for a given population, either observed, recommended, or maximum dose based on the type used.

@graph.rdfs:label: PriceComponentTypeEnumeration
@graph.name: PriceComponentTypeEnumeration
@graph.rdfs:comment: Enumerates different price components that together make up the total price for an offered product.

@graph.rdfs:label: ContactPoint
@graph.name: ContactPoint
@graph.rdfs:comment: A contact point—for example, a Customer Complaints department.

@graph.rdfs:label: hiringOrganization
@graph.name: hiringOrganization
@graph.rdfs:comment: Organization or Person offering the job position.

@graph.rdfs:label: prescribingInfo
@graph.name: prescribingInfo
@graph.rdfs:comment: Link to prescribing information for the drug.

@graph.rdfs:label: eligibleWithSupplier
@graph.name: eligibleWithSupplier
@graph.rdfs:comment: The supplier of the incentivized item/service for which the incentive is valid for such as a utility company, merchant, or contractor.

@graph.rdfs:label: BusinessEntityType
@graph.name: BusinessEntityType
@graph.rdfs:comment:
A business entity type is a conceptual entity representing the legal form, the size, the main line of business, the position in the value chain, or any combination thereof, of an organization or business person.

Commonly used values:

* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Business
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Enduser
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#PublicInstitution
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Reseller

@graph.rdfs:label: PoliticalParty
@graph.name: PoliticalParty
@graph.rdfs:comment: Organization: Political Party.

@graph.rdfs:label: biomechnicalClass
@graph.name: biomechnicalClass
@graph.rdfs:comment: The biomechanical properties of the bone.

@graph.rdfs:label: DigitalDocumentPermissionType
@graph.name: DigitalDocumentPermissionType
@graph.rdfs:comment: A type of permission which can be granted for accessing a digital document.

@graph.rdfs:label: OperatingSystem
@graph.name: OperatingSystem
@graph.rdfs:comment: System software that manages computer hardware and software resources, and provides common services for computer programs.

@graph.rdfs:label: MaximumDoseSchedule
@graph.name: MaximumDoseSchedule
@graph.rdfs:comment: The maximum dosing schedule considered safe for a drug or supplement as recommended by an authority or by the drug/supplement's manufacturer. Capture the recommending authority in the recognizingAuthority property of MedicalEntity.

@graph.rdfs:label: DoseSchedule
@graph.name: DoseSchedule
@graph.rdfs:comment: A specific dosing schedule for a drug or supplement.

@graph.rdfs:label: permitAudience
@graph.name: permitAudience
@graph.rdfs:comment: The target audience for this permit.

@graph.rdfs:label: circle
@graph.name: circle
@graph.rdfs:comment: A circle is the circular region of a specified radius centered at a specified latitude and longitude. A circle is expressed as a pair followed by a radius in meters.

@graph.rdfs:label: studyLocation
@graph.name: studyLocation
@graph.rdfs:comment: The location in which the study is taking/took place.

@graph.rdfs:label: cheatCode
@graph.name: cheatCode
@graph.rdfs:comment: Cheat codes to the game.

@graph.rdfs:label: labelDetails
@graph.name: labelDetails
@graph.rdfs:comment: Link to the drug's label details.

@graph.rdfs:label: billingAddress
@graph.name: billingAddress
@graph.rdfs:comment: The billing address for the order.

@graph.rdfs:label: parentTaxon
@graph.name: parentTaxon
@graph.rdfs:comment: Closest parent taxon of the taxon in question.

@graph.rdfs:label: dataFeedElement
@graph.name: dataFeedElement
@graph.rdfs:comment: An item within a data feed. Data feeds may have many elements.

@graph.rdfs:label: awayTeam
@graph.name: awayTeam
@graph.rdfs:comment: The away team in a sports event.

@graph.rdfs:label: positiveNotes
@graph.name: positiveNotes
@graph.rdfs:comment:
Provides positive considerations regarding something, for example product highlights or (alongside [[negativeNotes]]) pro/con lists for reviews.

In the case of a [[Review]], the property describes the [[itemReviewed]] from the perspective of the review; in the case of a [[Product]], the product itself is being described.

The property values can be expressed either as unstructured text (repeated as necessary), or if ordered, as a list (in which case the most positive is at the beginning of the list).

@graph.rdfs:label: governmentBenefitsInfo
@graph.name: governmentBenefitsInfo
@graph.rdfs:comment: governmentBenefitsInfo provides information about government benefits associated with a SpecialAnnouncement.

@graph.rdfs:label: serviceLocation
@graph.name: serviceLocation
@graph.rdfs:comment: The location (e.g. civic structure, local business, etc.) where a person can go to access the service.

@graph.rdfs:label: offers
@graph.name: offers
@graph.rdfs:comment: An offer to provide this item—for example, an offer to sell a product, rent the DVD of a movie, perform a service, or give away tickets to an event. Use [[businessFunction]] to indicate the kind of transaction offered, i.e. sell, lease, etc. This property can also be used to describe a [[Demand]]. While this property is listed as expected on a number of common types, it can be used in others. In that case, using a second type, such as Product or a subtype of Product, can clarify the nature of the offer.

@graph.rdfs:label: MediaEnumeration
@graph.name: MediaEnumeration
@graph.rdfs:comment: MediaEnumeration enumerations are lists of codes, labels etc. useful for describing media objects. They may be reflections of externally developed lists, or created at schema.org, or a combination.

@graph.rdfs:label: payload
@graph.name: payload
@graph.rdfs:comment:
The permitted weight of passengers and cargo, EXCLUDING the weight of the empty vehicle.

Typical unit code(s): KGM for kilogram, LBR for pound

* Note 1: Many databases specify the permitted TOTAL weight instead, which is the sum of [[weight]] and [[payload]]
* Note 2: You can indicate additional information in the [[name]] of the [[QuantitativeValue]] node.
* Note 3: You may also link to a [[QualitativeValue]] node that provides additional information using [[valueReference]].
* Note 4: Note that you can use [[minValue]] and [[maxValue]] to indicate ranges.

@graph.rdfs:label: measurementDenominator
@graph.name: measurementDenominator
@graph.rdfs:comment: Identifies the denominator variable when an observation represents a ratio or percentage.

@graph.rdfs:label: contactOption
@graph.name: contactOption
@graph.rdfs:comment: An option available on this contact point (e.g. a toll-free number or support for hearing-impaired callers).

@graph.rdfs:label: departureAirport
@graph.name: departureAirport
@graph.rdfs:comment: The airport where the flight originates.

@graph.rdfs:label: MusicVenue
@graph.name: MusicVenue
@graph.rdfs:comment: A music venue.

@graph.rdfs:label: WarrantyScope
@graph.name: WarrantyScope
@graph.rdfs:comment:
A range of services that will be provided to a customer free of charge in case of a defect or malfunction of a product.

Commonly used values:

* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Labor-BringIn
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#PartsAndLabor-BringIn
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#PartsAndLabor-PickUp

@graph.rdfs:label: monthsOfExperience
@graph.name: monthsOfExperience
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indicates the minimal number of months of experience required for a position.

@graph.rdfs:label: shippingOrigin
@graph.name: shippingOrigin
@graph.rdfs:comment: Indicates the origin of a shipment, i.e. where it should be coming from.

@graph.rdfs:label: itemDefectReturnFees
@graph.name: itemDefectReturnFees
@graph.rdfs:comment: The type of return fees for returns of defect products.

@graph.rdfs:label: dateRead
@graph.name: dateRead
@graph.rdfs:comment: The date/time at which the message has been read by the recipient if a single recipient exists.

@graph.rdfs:label: productionCompany
@graph.name: productionCompany
@graph.rdfs:comment: The production company or studio responsible for the item, e.g. series, video game, episode etc.

@graph.rdfs:label: SizeSpecification
@graph.name: SizeSpecification
@graph.rdfs:comment: Size related properties of a product, typically a size code ([[name]]) and optionally a [[sizeSystem]], [[sizeGroup]], and product measurements ([[hasMeasurement]]). In addition, the intended audience can be defined through [[suggestedAge]], [[suggestedGender]], and suggested body measurements ([[suggestedMeasurement]]).

@graph.rdfs:label: relevantOccupation
@graph.name: relevantOccupation
@graph.rdfs:comment: The Occupation for the JobPosting.

@graph.rdfs:label: subReservation
@graph.name: subReservation
@graph.rdfs:comment: The individual reservations included in the package. Typically a repeated property.

@graph.rdfs:label: department
@graph.name: department
@graph.rdfs:comment: A relationship between an organization and a department of that organization, also described as an organization (allowing different urls, logos, opening hours). For example: a store with a pharmacy, or a bakery with a cafe.

@graph.rdfs:label: ConfirmAction
@graph.name: ConfirmAction
@graph.rdfs:comment:
The act of notifying someone that a future event/action is going to happen as expected.

Related actions:

* [[CancelAction]]: The antonym of ConfirmAction.
